speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) whether there are long-term follow-up measures in schools to monitor the emotional and mental state of children and youths who have experienced sudden death of their peers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The students are taught coping strategies and encouraged to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Peers are also reminded to look out for and support one another.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I ask this because unless the teachers have sufficient information, they will be less equipped to support our children, our youths in overcoming the trauma.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: An example of the steps that schools have already taken would be reaching out to the bereaved family.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: A second example is what are the additional steps that the school will take.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, how do they intend to break the news to the affected students, making arrangements to assist students, staff and teachers to attend the wake.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Another thing that the teachers will be supported in terms of information is that schools will advise the teachers to direct any queries from the parents or the members of the public to the principal or designated staff.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It may be likely that the principal and staff may not have all the relevant information at the first meeting.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The teachers can also use this information to look out for students, watch out for affected students, and refer students who need additional support for help.
